summary: A criterion is marked passed when any one axe rule mapped to it passes on a page, and criterion results are upserted per page so the last page processed decides the stored status (a later not_applicable can replace an earlier passed). Only the first WCAG tag of a rule is used.
evidence: code: passesToCriterionResults, getWcagCriterion, upsertCriterionResult in the Tier 1 loop
resolution: aggregateAxeCriteria (checks/automated/index.ts) settles each criterion over all pages from every rule's outcome and every WCAG tag of the rule: passed only when each mapped rule passed or was inapplicable on every page and at least one passed somewhere; a violation or incomplete result on any page, in any order, leaves the status to the findings; all rules inapplicable everywhere is not_applicable. The scanner no longer upserts per page. On tuning-v5 this corrected 3.1.1 (not_applicable → passed: html-has-lang and html-lang-valid passed on 47 of 47 pages, html-xml-lang-mismatch inapplicable) and 3.3.2 (not_applicable → passed: form-field-multiple-labels passed on 2 of 47 pages, inapplicable elsewhere): the old loop wrote each page's passes and then its inapplicables, so the inapplicable row overwrote the pass on every page.

component: core/prompt-runner.ts (per-call usage and timings.json prompt stats); Analysis.llm_output.tokens_used
summary: The scanner records only the sum of input and output tokens per model call (tokensUsed = usage.input_tokens + usage.output_tokens), so the spend of a production scan can only be estimated: input and output are priced differently (3 vs 15 USD per million tokens for the model used). Proposed: record usage.input_tokens and usage.output_tokens (and cache read/creation tokens when present) per call, per prompt in timings.json, and in llm_output, and report a computed cost.
evidence: prompt-runner.ts: const tokensUsed = (response.usage?.input_tokens ?? 0) + (response.usage?.output_tokens ?? 0); scan 782f7078 timings.json shows 94 calls and 147,012 tokens with no split, so its cost could only be bounded ($0.44 if all input, $2.21 if all output) and estimated at about $0.77 from the eval record cost per call. The eval harness's own client already records the split (cache attempts carry usage and cost_usd).

component: checks/behavioral/keyboard.ts recordTabSequence (handle.boundingBox read right after each Tab); checks/behavioral/focus-order.ts analyzeFocusOrder
summary: Focus-order positions are viewport-relative boxes read immediately after each Tab. On a site with smooth scrolling (the Popfly site sets scroll-behavior: smooth) a Tab to a control beyond the first viewport starts a smooth scroll and the box is sampled mid-scroll, so the vertical deltas between stops depend on round-trip timing rather than on the layout. Any change to the per-stop timing moves focus_order_mismatch findings: the embed step-over (P2-034) adds one in-page evaluate per stop and moved 14 of them on tuning-v5 (5 re-keyed, 7 gone, 2 new), including two pages with no embed at all.
evidence: p004 /platform and p017 /company/jobs: the keyboard sweep is identical in replay-20261016T004003Z-84c628 (c157a07) and replay-20261016T004954Z-fcb1d7 (098dd72): 43 and 41 stops, exit cycle, same last element, retried no; neither page has an Instagram, TikTok or YouTube container; only the focus-order result differs (base: 2 issues diverging at index 12 and 1 issue at index 9; head: none, 3 of 3 repeats). Offline one-page sweeps from the tuning-v5 HAR at both commits read y = 355..435 for p004's stops 7-13 (all beyond the first viewport) across four runs, and on p017 a -283 px 'backward jump' from stop 9 to stop 10 that is stop 10 appearing higher in the viewport after the scroll. scroll-behavior: smooth appears in p004's DOM and in 6 stylesheets in its HAR. Within one commit the result is stable (7f0f3b and 84c628 agree on p004/p017; fcb1d7 3 of 3), so the shift is systematic, not flake.
candidate_fixes: (a) read positions as page coordinates (getBoundingClientRect plus scrollX/scrollY in the same evaluate) after the scroll settles

(b) inject html { scroll-behavior: auto !important } during the keyboard sweep so Tab focus scrolls instantly. Verify first that the injection does not change the skip-link check, which depends on Webflow's JS smooth scroll (Date-based), not on CSS scroll-behavior (P2-013).

On tuning-v5 (3 repeats) focus-order results are identical across repeats and backward jumps fell from 33 to 2; the 'large_gap' rule (> 500 px downward) then rose from 2 to 106 issues on 23 of 48 pages, because in page coordinates it only measures a stretch of page with no focusable content (e.g. /company/jobs: nav button to first job link, 1,324 px), so it was removed; backward jumps (> 200 px upward) and same-row leftward jumps remain, with each jump's page distance in measured_values.jump_distances_px. Remaining findings: /company/events and /company/press, one same-row leftward jump of 834 px each. Tests: smooth-scroll fixture (identical positions across loads, no issue), the removed rule, a backward jump still reported with its distance.

component: eval/transport (deny proxy egress accounting; replay.ts attempted_egress)
summary: A refused CONNECT to cdn.prod.website-files.com:443 (the site's own asset CDN) reaches the deny proxy outside page routing and is counted as attempted egress, which invalidates the replay. Seen in replay-20261016T045426Z-19c656 r1 (5 attempts; r2 and r3 none), replay-20261015T004242Z-b67ec8 r1 and r2, and both record runs (record-20261014T225224Z-d73465, record-20261014T233843Z-b10cba). A speculative preconnect by Chromium (inferred): no resource request misses the HAR, and the connect carries no path.
evidence: sites/t01-head-r1/summary.json of 19c656: 471 egress entries, 466 declared connects (instagram, openai, google, linkedin, youtube hosts) and 5 browser CONNECT attempts to cdn.prod.website-files.com:443 with har_misses 0, node_fetch_misses 0; totals attempted_egress 5 (observed). The host is served from the corpus HAR for every page.
proposed_fix: Treat a refused CONNECT to a host present in the corpus HAR as a declared hit (counted, not egress), since nothing left the machine and the host's resources are replayed from the HAR. Not fixed in fix batch 2 unless it invalidates another gate; then as its own eval-code commit.
